$comment: Hybrids (docs/genius-tree.md): the genius of someone whose play turned after it settled and before its first refinement. rule: at the first refinement a genius may turn toward the base whose nature fits the play best, if that fit is at least `min` and better than its own base's by `margin` (as a share of its own). The hybrid's tree is composed from the two bases: its paths are the first base's, their leans bent `bend` of the way toward the second's nature (half as far, then a quarter, then not at all, while two of its paths would be earned by the same play) and named by `path` ({adj} is the second's hybrid.adj, {name} the path's); in each path the prong furthest from the second's nature gives way to the second's prong nearest that path, carried across with its finishes and named by `carried` ({adj} is the first's hybrid.adj). kind names the hybrid itself ({adj} the second's, {name} the first base's). of: what a hybrid's path is the picture of ({of} is the first base's path's own; {first} and {second} the bases' names); the forms under it keep their own. sign: what a stranger would notice ({sign} is the form's own, where it is one of the first base's; {gift} the second's gift in words). A hybrid's form keeps the habit of the first base's form (a carried prong takes the habit of the prong it replaced). pairs: a pair written by hand, keyed first+second: its `name`, and `nodes` (by the id of the form of either base it came from: `name`, `text`, `of`, `sign`, `habit`) where the rule's words are not good enough.
